title: When the Signal Sings Revisited
premise: Ivo Okonkwo discovers his own name on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that was supposedly destroyed before he ever earned his wings — a ship whose hold contains not cargo but forty-one sleeping backups, one of which is a younger version of himself. The message the Meridian carries is a verified ceasefire protocol from the war's original architects, and both fleets will destroy it rather than let the other side inherit the peace. Ivo must choose between waking his backup — who remembers a different, truer version of their shared past — and delivering the message intact, knowing either act will cost him the loyalty of the crew who became his family. In the end he wakes the backup, splits the message between them, and delivers half to each fleet, forcing the truce by making peace something no single side can own.
about_author: Juniper Villalobos is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes about people caught between signals they can't ignore and families they can't quite trust. They live in a coastal town where the fog rolls in on schedule, and they insist this is relevant.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomalies
chapters.summary: Ivo Okonkwo, POV. During a routine customs scan in contested orbit, Ivo finds an unfamiliar name — his own birth name — on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship officially lost seven years ago. He hides the discovery from his captain. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: The Hold Nobody Opens
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. He bribes a dock clerk and learns the Meridian didn't sink — it was impounded, its hold sealed by fleet order. Flashbacks establish the backups he hauls as legitimate cargo and why they haunt him. Emotional beat: dread; the haunted man realizes the haunting has an address.

chapters.title: Crew of Small Loyalties
chapters.summary: First mate Sefa Adeyemi, POV. A portrait chapter: the freighter Kestrel's crew — Sefa, engineer Dov, teenage runner Pip — argue about taking a suspicious escort job near the Meridian's last known coordinates. Sefa quietly decides to protect Ivo from himself. Emotional beat: warmth; found family established before it's threatened.

chapters.title: Truce Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Fleet negotiator Captain Rhee, POV. The ceasefire expires in nineteen days; both fleets are rearming under cover of diplomacy. Rhee intercepts chatter about a 'verified protocol' aboard the Meridian and orders it recovered at any cost. Emotional beat: cold ambition; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Boarding the Ghost
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. The Kestrel docks with the drifting, dark Meridian. Inside: no bodies, no logs, but a hold full of active stasis pods — forty-one backups, including one labeled with Ivo's name and a date five years old. Emotional beat: vertigo; standing inside your own erased history.

chapters.title: The One Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Backup-Ivo, POV (woken briefly by a power surge). Fragmentary memories surface: the Meridian's real mission, a betrayal aboard, and a message encoded across the pods themselves. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief; a self that knows more than the original.

chapters.title: What Dov Found in the Wiring
chapters.summary: Dov, POV. Repairing the Meridian's power coupling, Dov discovers the message isn't stored — it's distributed through the pods' life-support signatures, unreadable unless all forty-one are awake simultaneously. He tells only Ivo. Emotional beat: complicity; knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: Rhee's Offer
chapters.summary: Rhee, POV. Rhee catches up to the Kestrel and offers Ivo immunity and a command for the ship's surrender, framing the message as fleet property. Ivo stalls. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a uniform; loyalty tested by legitimacy.

chapters.title: Pip's Question
chapters.summary: Pip, POV. Pip, having snooped, asks Ivo directly whether the sleeping man is him. Ivo lies badly. Pip keeps the secret but starts leaving notes in the navigation logs — questions about identity Ivo can't answer. Emotional beat: tenderness and fracture; children see through us.

chapters.title: The Betrayal Reconstructed
chapters.summary: Backup-Ivo, POV, via partial awakening. His memories assemble: the Meridian's architect-captain sabotaged her own message because she learned what peace would cost her faction — and the crew voted, fatally, to hide the truth in themselves. Emotional beat: tragic inheritance; the dead chose them as vessels.

chapters.title: Sefa Draws the Line
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Sefa confronts Ivo: wake the pods and the Kestrel becomes a military target, or walk away and stay safe. She demands a vote. Ivo refuses to vote against himself. Emotional beat: anger born of love; family fights hardest over survival.

chapters.title: Nineteen Becomes Nine
chapters.summary: Rhee, POV. A faction within Rhee's own fleet moves to seize the Meridian independently, forcing Rhee toward extremes. Rhee authorizes a kill-order contingency on the Kestrel. Emotional beat: escalation; even the schemer loses control of the scheme.

chapters.title: Waking Is a Vote
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Against Sefa's objection, Ivo begins sequential awakenings — each pod woken shares a fragment of the message and a memory, and each awakened backup must consent to carry it. Some refuse. Emotional beat: moral weight made physical; consent as cargo.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Say No
chapters.summary: Awakened backup Mara Voss, POV. One backup, a former diplomat, argues the message should die: the peace it encodes pardons war criminals, herself included. Her refusal splits the awakened group. Emotional beat: uncomfortable sympathy; justice versus mercy.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Dov, POV. Rhee's rogue faction attacks. The Kestrel takes damage; two awakened backups are killed, and with them fragments of the message are lost forever. Dov burns out his own implants keeping the remaining fragments synced. Emotional beat: sacrifice; the message now can never be whole.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. With fragments missing, delivery of the complete protocol is impossible. Backup-Ivo proposes the unthinkable: split what remains between the two fleets so neither holds enough to dictate terms — peace by mutual incompleteness. Emotional beat: desperate clarity; broken things making new shapes.

chapters.title: What Ivo Owes Himself
chapters.summary: Ivo and backup-Ivo, alternating POV. The two Ivos finally speak honestly: the original abandoned the mission that created the backups; the backup never got to live. They negotiate who delivers which half — and who gets to keep the name. Emotional beat: reckoning; identity as something shared, not owned.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Last Patience
chapters.summary: Rhee, POV. Truce expires in hours. Rhee, learning of the split plan, must decide whether to allow a peace she can't control or trigger the war she was built to prevent. Emotional beat: crisis of conviction; the gatekeeper at the gate.

chapters.title: Two Ships, Two Names
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Under fire, the Kestrel and the refitted Meridian launch in opposite directions, each carrying half the message and one Ivo. Sefa pilots one, Pip the other's nav seat. Emotional beat: terror and resolve; family divided on purpose to hold something together.

chapters.title: The Signal Sings
chapters.summary: Both Ivos, synchronized POV. Each delivers their fragment simultaneously to opposing fleet councils; neither side can verify alone, and mutual verification forces the armistice open. Rhee stands down her kill-order at the last second. Emotional beat: catharsis; the signal finally heard, imperfect and sufficient.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Forty
chapters.summary: Mara Voss, POV. The surviving awakened backups face judgment for the Meridian's buried crimes; Mara testifies to her own guilt and is spared to help build the tribunal. The message's missing fragments become permanent gaps the peace must live with. Emotional beat: sober hope; peace as ongoing work, not a gift.

chapters.title: Navigation Notes
chapters.summary: Pip, POV, framed as entries in the Kestrel's log. The two Ivos correspond across the new truce lines, signing letters with different names; Pip answers the questions once left in the nav logs. The Kestrel flies again, hauling ordinary cargo. Emotional beat: quiet continuation; inheritance chosen rather than received.
